Bread goes stale primarily because its starch molecules slowly rearrange themselves over time. This process is known as retrogradation and causes the crumb to become hard and dry. Moisture migrates from softer parts of the loaf toward the crust during this chemical change. The presence of sugar or fat can slightly delay staling by interfering with how the starch crystallizes. Freezing bread helps preserve its texture because it slows down the movement of water molecules within the starch structure. Ultimately, understanding that stale bread is still safe to eat just changes its physical properties due to starch behavior.

Afterward, the illumination decreases during the waning gibbous and third quarter phases before returning to darkness at the new moon again. This continuous pattern repeats every twenty-nine and a half days as Earth orbits the Sun with our Moon in tow. Understanding these stages helps us track time historically and appreciate the changing shadows on our night sky tonight.
